Part 2&3 人物 PEOPLE

Describe a friend from your childhood

描述你童年时期的一个朋友

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a friend from your childhood

  • Who he/she is (他/她是谁)
  • Where and how you met each other (你们在哪里以及怎么认识的)
  • What you often did together (你们经常一起做什么)
  • And explain what made you like him/her (并解释是什么让你喜欢他/她)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a friend from your childhood

I'd like to talk about my childhood friend Zeng, who was my classmate in primary school. We were in the same class from the first grade, and we actually sat next to each other for a couple of years, so we got to know each other really well. We met at school, in our classroom, and honestly, we became friends almost immediately. I remember he was one of the first people I talked to on my very first day, and after that we were basically inseparable. As for what we did together, we spent most of our free time playing games in the schoolyard. Our favourites were tag and hide-and-seek, and we'd run around until we were completely out of breath. Sometimes we'd also trade snacks at lunch, which sounds silly now, but it felt like a big deal back then. The reason I liked him so much was that he was just so much fun to be around. He always came up with new games and new ways to make me laugh, and he never made me feel left out. Looking back, I think he taught me how to enjoy the simple things in life. Unfortunately, we lost contact after we finished primary school, because we went to different middle schools. I still think about those days sometimes, and I'm grateful for the friendship we had.

讲童年好友 zeng，小学同班同桌，常一起玩抓人和捉迷藏；他有趣、从不让我落单，教会我享受简单快乐；小学毕业后去了不同中学就失去联系。

Q2Do you still keep in touch with your friends from childhood? Why or why not?

To be honest, I don't keep in touch with most of my childhood friends, and I think that's quite common. The main reason is that we went to different schools and gradually drifted apart, since we no longer shared the same daily life. I mean, when you're a child, friendship is built on being together every day, so once that disappears, it's hard to maintain the connection.

不常联系，因为去了不同学校、生活不再交集，慢慢疏远；孩子的友谊靠天天在一起维系。

Q3How important is childhood friendship to children?

I'd say childhood friendship is extremely important, probably more than most people realise. For one thing, it's how children learn social skills like sharing, cooperating and resolving conflicts. On top of that, having a close friend gives children a sense of security and belonging, which supports their emotional development. So I believe these early friendships shape how children relate to others later in life.

童年友谊极其重要：孩子借此学会分享、合作、解决冲突，朋友带来安全感和归属感，影响日后的人际关系。

Q4What do you think of communicating via social media?

From my perspective, social media has made communication much more convenient, since you can stay in touch with people across any distance. That said, I think it also has downsides, because messages can easily be misunderstood without tone of voice or facial expressions. So while it's a useful tool, I don't think it can fully replace the warmth of talking to someone in person.

社交媒体让沟通更方便、能跨距离联系；但缺少语气和表情容易误解，无法完全替代当面交流的温暖。

Q5Do you think online communication through social media will replace face-to-face communication?

I don't think it will completely replace face-to-face communication, although it will probably keep growing. The reason is that people naturally crave real human contact, and things like body language and eye contact simply can't be transmitted online. For important moments, like weddings or funerals, people will always want to be physically present. So I'd say online communication will complement, rather than replace, in-person interaction.

不会完全取代面对面交流：人天生渴望真实接触，肢体语言和眼神无法线上传递，重要场合人们仍会到场；线上是补充而非替代。

Q6What's the difference between having younger friends and older friends?

Generally speaking, younger friends tend to be more energetic and open to new ideas, whereas older friends usually offer more experience and practical advice. For example, an older friend might warn you about mistakes they've already made, while a younger friend is more likely to join you in trying something new. I think both are valuable, but they serve quite different purposes in your life.

年轻朋友更有活力、乐于尝试新事物；年长朋友经验丰富、能给出实用建议；两者各有价值、作用不同。

Q7Has technology changed people's friendships? How?

Yes, technology has changed friendships in quite significant ways. For one thing, it's now possible to maintain friendships across long distances, which wasn't easy before. However, I think the quality of interaction has changed too, because people often communicate through short messages rather than deep conversations. So friendships have become easier to maintain, but perhaps a bit shallower in some cases.

科技大幅改变了友谊：能跨距离维系友情，但交流常变成短消息而非深入对话，友谊更容易维持却可能更浅。
